title: Project test interpreter
summary: Tests run on the project's own Python, never Yoke's. yoke watch pytest uses the locked source environment in a Yoke checkout, uv run for a uv project (pyproject.toml beside uv.lock) or a declared test_environment, and otherwise reuses the running virtual environment when its resolved prefix lives inside the checkout, then tries the repo root's .venv. With neither environment it refuses with PROJECT-ENVIRONMENT-MISSING and names the setup_command capability that creates it. A Command case in another project's checkout puts that checkout's .venv first on PATH and sets VIRTUAL_ENV, so python -m pytest runs the project's tests; YOKE_PYTHON always names Yoke's interpreter. When lane dependency detection selects no install, it lists detected files instead of claiming none exist, preserves missing-installer diagnostics, and prints the projects capability-settings set command for setup_command. A bare pyproject.toml needs a setup_command or a uv.lock for uv provisioning; the diagnostic names missing uv when it is absent from PATH. Declare setup_command once at project level using the project's documented environment command backed by its lockfile or toolchain script. This requires project authority; without it, ask steering or the operator. Lane prepare runs the declared command automatically; do not hand-prepare each lane. Rerun lane prepare after declaration, then retry tests. The public worktree guide teaches this project decision; onboarding detection does not declare it.
